newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's real rises 0.21 percent on dollar inflows.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's real rises 0.21 percent on dollar inflows.

text.p: Brazil's real rose 0.21 percent to close at 1.0185 against the greenback on dollar inflows in the commercial foreign exchange market, dealers said.

Preliminary figures for commercial and financial foreign exchange contracts showed a Friday surplus of $95 million in the late afternoon. It was the first surplus after three days of deficits, dealers said.
The second half of the month should register more dollar inflows, they added, citing recent Eurobond issues.
Some dealers also believed the Central Bank could lower the real-dollar mini-band at the beginning of the next week. The current mini-band was set on Tuesday between 1.018 and 1.023 reais per dollar.
In the interbank forex floating rate market, the real closed steady at 1.0237 to the dollar.
In the illegal parallel market, the real ended unchanged at 1.034 per greenback, traders said.
